newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia coffee stable, trade dull on low stocks.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia coffee stable, trade dull on low stocks.

text.p: Indonesian Robusta coffee prices were generally stable on Monday, with low stocks before the harvest begins in March keeping activity thin, traders said.

They said the local price was quoted at 3,450-3,550 rupiah/kg in the key growing region of Lampung in South Sumatra, unchanged from a week ago. The export price was also generally stable at $1,500/tonne fob Lampung.

"Prices are relatively good overseas, but we don't have much coffee to sell because the harvest doesn't begin until next month," one trader said. "There are some who are selling forward, especially June, but it's not much."

Traders also said they were concerned over the widening price differential between arabica and robusta. The arbitrage between the two varieties widened to 105 cents per lb basis March in London from 40 cents in December.
London benchmark May touched an intraday high of $1,705 a tonne last Friday before ending at $1,675, up $15 on the day.
One local trader said he expected London to open $50 lower later on Monday on profit taking.
"The market has gone crazy," he said. "There's a big difference between arabica and robusta. New York is going one way, and London is going another."
Another trader esimated that there were less than 20,000 tonnes of coffee in the hands of exporters and middleman in Indonesia at the moment, adding that buyers were scarce.
"Local sellers are offering at relatively high prices while buyers are looking for big discounts to London prices," the trader said. "The market's very confusing."
Traders also said they did not expect Indonesia's decision to cut exports by 150,000 bags in the first half of this year to weigh on the market, as exports only begin in earnest in June.
